transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining this planning roundtable. As you know, the middle school has proposed a six-week peer-tutoring program for students in grades 6 through 8, and I've asked each of you here today so we can review the draft plan together before I make a final decision. The current proposal calls for two adult supervisors, Google Classroom for session communication, student-selected tutor pairings, and paper consent forms collected before the program begins. I'd like to go around the table and hear from each of you on any concerns or recommendations you have related to your area of expertise. Let's start with the teacher — what are your thoughts on the academic side of this program?

These restrictions are currently recorded only in confidential counseling files, so no one else at the table would have been aware of them. Tutor pairings must instead be assigned and monitored by me as the counselor, so I can ensure that no student is paired with someone they have a no-contact restriction with. I recommend that the plan be revised to replace student-selected pairings with counselor-assigned, counselor-monitored pairings.
